input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Carvana

output.company: Carvana Co. (NYSE: CVNA); consolidated reporting group. Assessment as of 2026-11-09.

ownership.value: Publicly traded, founder/family-controlled company, not identified as PE-backed. The 2026 proxy identifies Ernest C. Garcia II, Ernest C. Garcia III and their controlled entities as the Garcia Parties and reports more than 50% of combined voting power, making Carvana a NYSE controlled company. No recent change of control was verified.

financials.metric: Total liquidity resources (includes additional debt capacity and unpledged securities; not all committed cash)
Net cash provided by operating activities
Tax receivable agreement liability (separate from reported debt)

debt_events.summary: August 2026 refinancing: $1.660 billion Term Loan B used with cash to redeem all $1.660 billion principal of 2030 secured notes for $1.711 billion, including $50 million premium and $1 million accrued interest. New loan matures 2033-08-14; SOFR plus 2.25% option, approximately 6.1% effective interest rate; no financial maintenance covenants. Substantially all assets of the borrower and guarantors secure it, ranking pari passu with remaining secured notes.

During Q3, Ally finance-receivable purchase commitment increased to up to $8 billion through July 2027; another loan purchase agreement extended through January 2028 and increased by $500 million, with conditional automatic extension to July 2028. One short-term revolving facility extended through August 2027. Receivable-sale commitments are not unrestricted cash revolvers.

Company reported compliance with all debt covenants. Part II Item 3 reported no defaults upon senior securities; this filing disclosure does not establish the absence of all possible payment disputes.

Historical, outside the last 12 months: the 2026 10-Q dates the notes exchange to September 2023. S&P classified the completed restructuring as distressed and tantamount to default, lowering the issuer to D at that time; approximately $5.5 billion unsecured notes were exchanged for approximately $4.2 billion secured notes. This is historical default treatment, not its current rating.

credit_ratings.summary: S&P: BB- issuer credit rating, positive outlook, expressly unchanged in this update; proposed secured term loan rated BB. On 2026-03-03 S&P affirmed BB-/Positive and upgraded existing senior-secured debt to BB; unsecured debt remained B. Latest opened issuer confirmation, not a guarantee of no subsequent change.

Fitch: first-time BB- Long-Term Issuer Default Rating; stable outlook reported in its action announcement and corroborating dated rating-action record. This new rating falls within the preceding 12 months.

Moody's, as reported by Cbonds on 2026-06-25: long-term local-currency rating upgraded to B3 from Caa1; positive outlook. Secondary reporting only; a current Moody's corporate-family rating could not be verified directly.

A separate Cbonds record reports Moody's long-term foreign-currency rating upgraded to B1 from B2; positive outlook. Its different classification and rating are preserved rather than treated as interchangeable with the B3 record; direct agency reconciliation is unavailable.

missing_fields: credit_ratings: directly verified current Moody’s corporate-family rating and reconciliation of secondary B3/B1 classifications
payment_behaviour: verified supplier-payment ageing, current trade references or systematic late-payment reports
payment_behaviour: confirmed supplier liens, judgments or established nonpayment; primary pleadings and legal-entity identity for Texas collection case
distress_signals: verified recent layoffs, hiring freezes, facility closures, CFO departures, auditor changes or large customer losses
ownership: any recent change of control after the proxy date
output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-11-09, elevated rather than high: the latest 10-Q shows $3.049 billion cash, $5.120 billion committed liquidity and $714 million quarterly operating income, plus covenant compliance and management's one-year funding assessment ([Q3 2026 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000067/cvna-20260930.htm)). Nevertheless, $5.161 billion reported debt, a separate $2.130 billion tax receivable agreement liability, extensive secured-creditor claims and speculative-grade BB- issuer ratings leave meaningful refinancing and unsecured-counterparty risk ([10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000067/cvna-20260930.htm); [S&P](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3605857); [Fitch](https://www.fitchratings.com/entity/carvana-co-97311003)). Historical consumer payment/title failures and the distressed 2023 exchange warrant caution, but do not establish current insolvency or a present supplier default ([Connecticut AG](https://portal.ct.gov/ag/press-releases/2025-press-releases/attorney-general-tong-announces-settlement-with-carvana-following-hundreds-of-consumer-complaints); [S&P historical exchange](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/12839346)).

distress_signals.summary: Liquidity mitigant: management stated working capital, operating cash flows and expected continued or new financing arrangements should fund operations for at least one year from financial-statement issuance (2026-10-28). This is management guidance dependent partly on financing, not a cash-only runway calculation.

Ongoing legal/regulatory disputes include consumer protection and vehicle titling/registration claims; unresolved legal matters accrued at $11 million. Filing warns adverse developments could materially affect business, financial condition or cash flows. Accrual is not an estimate of maximum exposure.

CFO Dive reported short-seller allegations about related-party disclosures and earnings; CFO Mark Jenkins rejected them and said the reporting was accurate. Allegations and predictions of auditor resignation are not established accounting violations or an actual auditor departure.

Grant Thornton signed an unmodified fair-presentation opinion on 2025 consolidated financial statements and an effective internal-control opinion as of 2025-12-31, stating it had served since 2015. The opened audit opinion contains no going-concern qualification; this is not assurance against subsequent deterioration.

payment_behaviour.summary: Historical consumer-payment signal, outside the last 12 months: Connecticut Attorney General announced a $1.5 million settlement after complaints including delayed seller payments and trade-in loan payoffs, alongside title/registration delays. Terms comprised $1 million restitution and $500,000 state penalty, with $250,000 suspended for compliance. This establishes consumer counterparty-performance concerns, not a supplier-credit default.

Possible commercial collection signal: a Collin County, Texas docket listing names "Carvana" among defendants in National Wholesale Supply v. Tarrant Electric & Heating and others, classified as commercial/trade debt collection and shown open. Underlying court documents were unavailable; precise Carvana legal-entity identity, liability, amount, judgment and payment outcome are unverified. Do not treat as a confirmed Carvana Co. default.
